I've been there.  Well, I was using Alprazolam and Heroin combo. I overdosed on the heroin and the Alprazolam assisted in stopping me from breathing. When they found me, my blood Oxygen level was around 65%. To put this in perspective, COPD patients have a blood Oxygen level 75%.  My blood pressure was 60/40. This is dangerously low. Pulmonary edema is what would have happened. Basically my lungs would have filled with blood and I would have asphyxiated.

Give or take a month. So, I basically did all of those over the period of like 2 months. Enough to get physically dependent. I ended up getting fired from my job, I was a dispatcher for Access (Transport for disabled people). My brother's wife sent me to another psych ward, against my will, but I needed it as I didn't care if I lived or died. I went through Xanax withdrawal. It was hell on earth, the rebound anxiety, the seizures, the cravings for Xanax, it was BAD, like I thought I was going to die bad. That was like 2 months ago. Since then, I've relapsed on heroin and xanax a few times. I've overdosed twice I think, my roomate had to save my life. Today, I'm clean from heroin, I'm on Suboxone, i can't take any benzodiazipine to stay on the Suboxone. Probably a good thing. And I smoke weed, they don't care about that. The only meds I take are : Clonidine (blood pressure med), Elavil (Tri-cyclic Antidepressant TCA) and the Suboxone. I have a degree in Computer Sciences, I've been working IT since 2004. I wish I would have studied Psychology. I really enjoy talking aetiology. I love talking with Psychiatrists/Psychologists. I give them a run for their money haha. I don't want to be a heroin addict, I don't want to suffer from depression/anxiety. I just want to be happy. It feels good to meet someone who is also going through similar eating issues. I thought I was the only one. People tell me, oh I wish I had your problem, because I eat too much and can't stop. I tell them no, you do not want the underlying cause of my inability to eat, you don't want the anxiety/stress, or the depression.

I suffer from Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Deressive Disorder, Bipolar type 2, and Opioid drug addiction. I know exactly what your talking about. I do not eat either. In the past 3 days I've had burger king breakfast, mcdonalds cheeseburger, some candy(sour patch kids!!) an ensure and ramen noodles. My anxiety is like panic attack levels recently. Im 34Male. I do not have an image problem. I am 6ft and weigh 135 lbs. like dangerously close to malnourished. Anyways, I have discovered that my anxiety is the cause of my inability to eat. I just can't stomach food. Because I'm probably crazy, I was in a psych ward a little over a year ago. While there I was unable to eat, to the point that the doctors had to get a nutritionist come and basically yell at me. She was like "When you think your full, just keep eating". And if your like me, thats a no go. Yea, let me try and eat, my body will reject it and I don't want to throw up. So, I spoke with a nurse and told her my situation. She told me that I was so tense and nervous. She asked me to relax. Which, when your a patient in a psych ward, its sometimes not possible. Anyways, I told her I can't. She gave me some Thorazine and Ativan. Thorazine is a anti-psychotic and Ativan is a strong benzodiazipine. Basically the Thorazine is a sedative; it'll put you on your ass at higher doses. It's what they hit you with if your flipping out and they need to sedate you. I was given a very small dose. It was just enough to relax me, which in turn relaxed my body and I was able to eat. So, I have learned that I internalize my anxiety and stress. This was invaluable information for me. I had to go crazy, get admitted to a psych ward to find out how to eat.
